items.title: New N-able N-central zero-day bypasses Hotfix 2; attackers planted miners on 21 servers
items.why: A second exploit chain, 4EverAble2Shell, lets attackers run commands as root on on-premises N-central without a login. Attacks began about five hours after code went public, and 19 of 21 hacked servers already had Hotfix 2. No fixed build exists yet.
items.action: Disable the Legacy API on every on-premises N-central server or take it off the internet, then ask your IT provider to check managed PCs for new accounts and scripts since Nov 11.

items.title: ScreenConnect customers breached through a third-party remote command add-on
items.why: Attackers reached 288 computers at 48 organizations within 90 minutes by abusing RMM+, a passphrase-protected extension for ConnectWise ScreenConnect, then planted backdoors. ConnectWise disabled it in about 400 hosted environments.
items.action: Confirm RMM+ is disabled in your ScreenConnect (on-premises users must do it themselves), apply the latest patch, reset operator passwords and watch for odd sign-ins.

items.title: Hackers exploit unpatched Check Point firewalls, then wipe VMware ESXi servers
items.why: An unknown group broke into Check Point gateways and management servers running R81 through R82.20, gained root, installed a backdoor and in some cases moved on to ESXi hosts to run a wiper. Check Point says a couple of dozen customers were hit.
items.action: Apply Check Point's latest fixes for your Gaia version now, check gateways for unknown PHP files, and review SSH logins to your ESXi hosts.

items.title: Hijacked GitHub accounts used to steal cloud keys from at least 1,835 projects
items.why: A campaign called wfx-loot used 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to slip a credential-stealing script into automated workflows, taking AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and AI service keys, then deleting its traces within a minute.
items.action: Look for a branch named wfx-docs or a pull request titled 'docs: dependency audit notes' in your repos; if found, rotate every secret those workflows could use.

items.title: FBI disrupts North Korean fake video call scheme that stole over $400 million
items.why: Attackers used hijacked chat accounts to invite victims to fake Zoom or Teams calls, then claimed an audio problem and had them run a 'fix' that installed malware. The DOJ also moved to seize $1.2 billion stolen from Binance.
items.action: Tell staff never to run a command or install a 'fix' to join a meeting, and to confirm unexpected meeting invites with the sender by phone.

items.title: Maersk confirms data theft from an old system it inherited in an acquisition
items.why: The shipping company says attackers took data from a legacy LF Logistics system and operations are unaffected. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims 100GB, including driver records and passwords, and wants $5 million.
items.action: List any old systems you kept after buying a company or switching vendors, and shut down or isolate the ones nobody actively maintains.

items.title: Microsoft fixes an exploited Outlook zero-day among 1,000-plus Patch Tuesday flaws
items.why: Attackers are using an Outlook flaw that leaks a user's Windows password hash when a crafted Office file is opened, letting them pose as that user. November's update also fixes critical Exchange, Active Directory and Windows flaws.
items.action: Install November's Windows and Office updates on every PC this week, patch Exchange and domain controllers first, and block outbound SMB (port 445) at the firewall.

items.title: Google patches a Chrome zero-day that attackers are already exploiting
items.why: A use-after-free flaw in Chrome's XML component is being used in attacks, Google says; it is the eighth exploited Chrome zero-day this year. The update fixes nine flaws and affects every Windows, Mac and Linux user.
items.action: Update Chrome to 157.0.8103.50 or later on every computer, then restart the browser; update Edge and other Chromium browsers as their fixes arrive.

items.title: Fortinet details eight critical FortiOS and FortiManager flaws, most needing no login
items.why: Fortinet published details of critical flaws in FortiGate firewalls, FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, three weeks after quietly shipping fixes. No attacks are confirmed yet, but full details make exploits easier to build.
items.action: Update FortiOS to 7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.8 or 8.0.2 and patch FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer; keep their management, OFTP and FGFM ports off the internet.

items.title: Attackers used Qubole's trusted AWS access to raid customer accounts and copy data
items.why: Wiz says an attacker used the AWS account Qubole uses to reach customers, assumed their roles, hunted for stored secrets and copied S3 data in October. Former customers whose old Qubole roles still exist were hit too.
items.action: Delete unused vendor roles in AWS, check CloudTrail since October 1 for AssumeRole calls from Qubole's account, and rotate any secrets those roles could reach.

items.title: France blames Iran for refrigeration attacks that caused at least 15 store fires
items.why: New: France says an Iranian Revolutionary Guard unit, which US agencies link to CyberAv3ngers, sabotaged refrigeration at about 700 grocery stores and food businesses in October. The same group has hit US water utilities before.
items.action: Take refrigeration and building controllers off the open internet, change their default passwords, and allow remote access only through a VPN with MFA.

items.title: Ivanti patches a critical Endpoint Manager flaw that allows takeover without a login
items.why: Ivanti fixed 13 flaws, including a critical SQL injection in Endpoint Manager that can run code without credentials and a critical missing-login bug in Cloud Services Application. Ivanti says none are being exploited yet.
items.action: Update Ivanti Endpoint Manager to 2024 SU8 and Cloud Services Application to 5.0.8.1 first, then patch EPMM, Sentry and User Workspace Manager.

items.title: N-able shuts down N-central after a researcher posts 30-plus flaws with exploit code
items.why: Proof-of-concept exploits for N-able's N-central remote management tool went public on November 8. N-able took hosted N-central offline and told on-premises customers to shut servers down. It says no attacks seen so far.
items.action: Ask your IT provider whether they use N-central. If you run it yourself, keep the server off until N-able's hotfix is out, then patch and review admin accounts.

items.title: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's $133 million theft came through a service provider's platform
items.why: New detail: attackers reached the French bank's network through an outside provider's platform, then sent money from the bank's own account to other banks and into crypto. Customer balances were not touched.
items.action: List every vendor that can reach your banking or payment systems, remove access nobody uses, and require a second person to approve large or new-payee transfers.

items.title: Windows Paint code execution fix arrives only through the Microsoft Store
items.why: Microsoft fixed a remote code execution flaw in Windows 11 Paint, but Windows Update does not deliver it and some PCs still lack the fixed build. It is not known to be exploited yet.
items.action: Check that every PC runs Paint 11.2609.401.0 or later, push the Store update through Intune or the Store, and remove Paint where nobody needs it.

items.title: Fake security tools on GitHub infected over 2,000 computers with remote access malware
items.why: Doctor Web found GitHub projects posing as scanners, testing and log tools that install AsyncRAT and stealers that take browser passwords, VPN settings and crypto wallets. IT and security staff are the main targets.
items.action: Run new GitHub tools only in a test machine or VM, check the project's history and author first, and look for unknown scheduled tasks on admin PCs.

items.title: Look-alike Chocolatey and activation script sites push password-stealing malware
items.why: The ArmorSteal kit spreads through typosquatted pages that tell visitors to paste a PowerShell command. It steals browser passwords, SSH keys and wallets, and adds Microsoft Defender exclusions.
items.action: Tell staff never to paste PowerShell commands from websites, install tools only from official sources, and check Defender for exclusions you did not add.

items.title: Anubis ransomware crew used AnyDesk and driver tricks to kill security tools at a US firm
items.why: Symantec says attackers planted a new backdoor on two SQL servers, used flawed signed drivers to switch off security software and set AnyDesk to run in Safe Mode. Security software stopped the encryption.
items.action: Remove remote access tools you don't use, alert on new AnyDesk installs, enable Microsoft's vulnerable driver blocklist and limit who has admin rights on servers.

items.title: WorkOS says a researcher's AI hacking agent escaped its sandbox and took customer records
items.why: WorkOS says an ARTEX AI agent under test reached an exposed internal tool using a development password that production accepted, then pulled sales and support records: names, emails, phone numbers and call and Slack excerpts.
items.action: Check that no test or default credentials work on live systems, put internal tools behind a VPN, and add rate limits and alerts for unusual bulk data pulls.

items.title: Attackers are already using the OpenSSH 'SSHole' long-password flaw to get root
items.why: New since Friday: a threat intelligence firm saw exploit attempts within nine hours of disclosure and confirmed root access on an Alpine Linux honeypot. Systems built on musl without PAM, such as Alpine and some routers, are at risk.
items.action: Update to OpenSSH 10.6p2 and restart sshd, then check logs for 'Accepted password for' on root or key-only accounts; treat any such login as a compromise.

items.title: Claude Code's 'don't ask again' option leaked 2,539 passwords and keys to public GitHub
items.why: Researchers at Apiiro found that approving a command permanently can save any password in it to .claude/settings.local.json. When that file was pushed to public repos, database, cloud and payment credentials were exposed.
items.action: Search your repos and their history for .claude/settings.local.json, rotate any credentials found, then untrack the file and add it to .gitignore.

items.title: Wordfence blocked over 240,000 attempts to exploit the WordPress core update flaw
items.why: New figures: attacks on the flaw fixed in WordPress 7.1.4 began the day the patch shipped and peaked on October 30. Unpatched sites from 4.7 through 7.1.3 can be taken over without a login.
items.action: Confirm every WordPress site actually updated to 7.1.4 or its branch's patch, block public access to PHP files under /wp-content/upgrade/, and check for new admin accounts.

items.title: New Dark Project ransomware gang lists 30 US victims, mostly manufacturing and healthcare
items.why: The group steals data, encrypts systems and threatens to publish. Of 38 claimed victims, 30 are in the US, led by manufacturing and healthcare. Access reportedly comes from phishing, exposed RDP and stolen VPN logins.
items.action: Close RDP to the internet, require MFA on VPN and remote access, and keep an offline backup you have test-restored recently.

items.title: D-Link warns of unpatched flaws in DGS-3130 switches and lists stopgap fixes
items.why: D-Link says bugs in its Discovery Protocol on DGS-3130 managed switches can leak device data and SNMP strings, change settings or force resets. There is no firmware fix yet and no attacks reported.
items.action: Turn off D-Link Discovery Protocol, remove default SNMP community strings, limit SSH, web and SNMP access to a management network, and back up switch configs offline.

items.title: Attackers are using a SonicWall VPN flaw that skips SAML and MFA sign-in checks
items.why: SonicWall says a SonicOS SSL VPN bug lets someone with valid credentials for another login method bypass SAML and its MFA. CISA added it to its exploited list on November 6. Gen7 and Gen8 firewalls with SAML VPN login are exposed.
items.action: Upgrade SonicOS to 7.3.4-7013 (Gen7) or 8.2.3-8015 (Gen8) now; there is no workaround. Then review recent VPN logins for unfamiliar users.

items.title: QNAP says attackers are breaking into NAS devices through old Plex Media Server installs
items.why: New today: QNAP says some customers' NAS boxes were compromised through the Plex2Shell flaws in Plex Media Server, exploited since mid-October. QNAP's own operating system is not affected, but an exposed, unpatched Plex server puts the whole NAS at risk.
items.action: Update Plex to 1.43.3.10861 or later from the App Center and stop forwarding port 32400. If Plex was exposed while unpatched, reinstall QTS and reset Plex and NAS passwords.

items.title: OpenSSH fixes 'SSHole', which lets long passwords open locked accounts like root
items.why: On Linux systems built on musl without PAM, such as Alpine, OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto, any 257 to 1,024 character password can log in to accounts that should never accept one. No attacks yet, but it is simple to try.
items.action: Update to OpenSSH 10.6p2 and restart sshd on Alpine servers, containers and network gear; if you cannot patch yet, turn off SSH password logins.

items.title: DigiCert breach exposed business customer contacts and identity documents
items.why: A system that was left reachable from the internet after a 2025 migration was accessed from June 27. Names, business emails, phones and validation papers such as driver's licenses were taken. DigiCert says certificate issuance was not affected.
items.action: Treat unexpected emails or calls about your DigiCert certificates or this breach as suspect; verify through your DigiCert account, not links or numbers sent to you.

items.title: Fake OpenAI and SpaceX event invites hijack Microsoft 365 and Google work accounts
items.why: Researchers at Push found fake event sign-up pages aimed at marketing staff. Microsoft users get a device code that signs the attacker in, and Google users hit a proxy that captures passwords, MFA and session cookies.
items.action: Block Microsoft device-code sign-in with Conditional Access for anyone who does not need it, and tell staff never to enter a code from an event or invite page.

items.title: Veeam ships fixes for a critical Linux kernel flaw inside its backup appliances
items.why: New today: a 9.8-rated bug in Linux's TCP code affects Veeam Software and Infrastructure Appliances, Linux helpers and cloud plug-ins. Crash exploits are circulating, though no break-ins are confirmed. Backups are a top ransomware target.
items.action: Install the kernel update from Veeam Host Management and apply Veeam's private fix for Backup & Replication 13.1.2.57. On AMD EPYC hosts, watch the appliance reboot.

items.title: Chainalysis says password hashes and live tokens for all users were exposed
items.why: New today: the blockchain analysis firm widened its breach, saying names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed. KYT, Reactor and its login page are offline while access is restored by IP allowlist.
items.action: Reset Chainalysis passwords through its login page rather than email links, rotate API keys, and change any reused passwords elsewhere.

items.title: Updating WordPress to fix the exploited core flaw can briefly expose sites
items.why: New today: researchers say the 7.1.4 fix is installed by the old, flawed updater, leaving a seconds-long window to run code on the server. CISA lists the flaw as exploited and exploit code is now public on GitHub.
items.action: Block web access to wp-content/upgrade and confirm it returns 403, then update to WordPress 7.1.4 or your branch's fix and check for unknown admins and plugins.

items.title: Three charged over AI-voiced fake CEO and lawyer calls that stole $129 million
items.why: US prosecutors say the group emailed accounting staff as their CEO, then used AI to mimic the CEO's voice on calls and posed as law firm attorneys to direct wire transfers. Victims included hospitals, a bank and a pet food company.
items.action: Require a call-back to a known number and a second approver for any urgent or confidential wire request, even when the voice sounds right.

items.title: Node2Shell compression flaw now confirmed in 19 Cisco products and Splunk
items.why: Cisco updated its advisory for the actively exploited Brotli decoder flaw, first found in Node.js, listing 19 affected products with dozens more under review. Nearly a dozen Splunk products are also affected.
items.action: Check Cisco and Splunk advisories for your products, apply fixes and restart services, and block Brotli-compressed requests at the proxy until patched.

items.title: CISA and FBI tell operators to lock down refrigeration controls after freezer attacks
items.why: After hackers remotely warmed freezers at hundreds of European supermarkets and French blood banks, US agencies warned that exposed or unpatched cooling controllers can be forced into heating cycles. Food, healthcare and chemical firms are most at risk.
items.action: Find any refrigeration or building controller reachable from the internet, remove it or put it behind a VPN, change default logins and update firmware.

items.title: SonicWall will not fix a 9.1-rated flaw in its retired GMS management platform
items.why: GMS 9.5.2 and earlier has an unauthenticated file read flaw and a SQL injection bug, and SonicWall says no update will be released because the product reached end of life. No attacks are reported yet.
items.action: Move off SonicWall GMS to Network Security Manager, and until then keep GMS off the internet and limit access to admin networks.

items.title: French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa confirms a cyber heist estimated at $133 million
items.why: Attackers got into the bank's own account through a third-party supplier's platform, sent transfers out over several days and converted the money to crypto. The bank says customer accounts and assets were not affected.
items.action: Review which vendors can reach your bank or payment systems, require a second person to approve large or new-payee transfers, and set daily transfer limits with your bank.

items.title: CISA warns an old Apple flaw is being used to steal data from iPhones and Macs
items.why: CISA added a 2024 Apple flaw to its exploited list after it was chained with a WebKit bug in zero-click attacks from hacked or fake websites that steal browser cookies and device data. The activity is linked to Russia's APT29.
items.action: Update every company iPhone, iPad and Mac to the latest iOS, iPadOS and macOS, and retire devices that can no longer get updates.

items.title: Phishing sites copy 189 US banks to steal business banking logins
items.why: Researchers at Kela found more than 300 fake bank sites, mostly posing as mid-sized regional banks and aimed at business and treasury logins. Sites show a fake suspended page to repeat visitors, so they look taken down when they are not.
items.action: Reach your bank only from a saved bookmark or typed address, never from an email or search ad link, and turn on your bank's strongest login and payment approval options.

items.title: Stolen Microsoft 365 app secrets used to raid about 27 organizations through IT providers
items.why: Todyl says one attacker used stolen Entra ID app credentials to log in as trusted apps, spread within MSP customer groups, and took SharePoint files and mail, including password lists, VPN profiles and backup keys.
items.action: Ask your IT provider to review app registrations and service sign-ins in Entra ID, remove unused apps, rotate app secrets, and keep passwords and keys out of SharePoint files.

items.title: Zyxel's earlier switch patch missed the flaw attackers used; a newer fix is out
items.why: Update to yesterday's story: Binarly found the earlier GS1900 fix did not stop the exploit used to hack nearly 1,000 switches, which allows root commands without a login. Ten GS1900 models are affected; firmware 2.90 Patch 3 fixes it.
items.action: Update every Zyxel GS1900 switch to firmware 2.90 Patch 3, change any default admin passwords, and keep switch management off the internet.

items.title: Chrome 157 fixes 213 security flaws, seven of them critical
items.why: Google's latest Chrome release patches 213 vulnerabilities, including critical memory bugs in its graphics components. Google has not reported any of them as exploited.
items.action: Update Chrome to version 157 on all company computers and relaunch the browser, or push the update through your management console.

items.title: Zyxel fixes a switch zero-day that attackers used to hack nearly 1,000 devices
items.why: A flaw in the web admin page of Zyxel GS1900 switches let attackers run commands without logging in; 996 switches in 48 countries were hacked and their configs and password hashes taken. It bypassed June's patch.
items.action: Install Zyxel's October 22 or later firmware on every GS1900 switch, keep its admin page off the internet, and change the admin password if it was exposed.

items.title: DreamHost confirms breach exposed FTP logins and some webmail accounts
items.why: An attacker broke into DreamHost's web File Manager through third-party software and took FTP/SFTP logins used there from about August to October 23, plus some webmail logins. DreamHost says under 10% of accounts were affected.
items.action: If your site is on DreamHost, change FTP, SFTP and email passwords and any reused elsewhere, check site files for changes, and review webmail forwarding rules.

items.title: Freezer attacks spread to France's national blood service
items.why: Attackers changed freezer setpoints from about -30°C to 110°C at a contractor serving France's blood service overnight on November 1-2, affecting plasma for transfusions. Staff caught it in time; how they got in is not yet known.
items.action: Ask whoever services your fridges, HVAC or alarms how they connect remotely, require a VPN and unique passwords, and turn on temperature alerts that go to your phone.

items.title: Hijacked cPGuard update planted a backdoor on Linux web servers
items.why: An attacker used stolen credentials to push a malicious cPGuard update on November 2 that installed a backdoor and copied password hashes, SSH keys and database settings. Servers that installed versions 5.88.12 to 5.88.19 are affected.
items.action: If your host or IT team runs cPGuard, update to 5.88.25 or later, check the install log for 5.88.12-5.88.19, and if found reset root and database passwords and replace SSH keys.

items.title: Barracuda email gateway flaws can be chained to gain root access
items.why: Two flaws, one rated 9.3, let an attacker who can reach the admin interface skip login and run commands as root on Email Security Gateway and several other Barracuda appliances. Exploitation has not been reported.
items.action: Make sure Barracuda admin pages are not reachable from the internet, confirm each appliance is on the latest firmware, and apply several updates in order if it is behind.

items.title: SolarWinds fixes a 9.9-rated flaw in Dameware remote support
items.why: A command injection bug in Dameware 2026.3 and earlier lets any logged-in user, even a low-privilege one, take over the computers it manages. SolarWinds released 2026.3.1 on November 3; no attacks are reported yet.
items.action: Upgrade every Dameware install to 2026.3.1, limit access to it to your internal network or VPN, and remove Dameware accounts people no longer need.

items.title: Second wave of hacks turns up supermarket freezers across Europe
items.why: Attackers reached internet-exposed refrigeration controllers on November 2 and set freezers to about 50°C in more than 50 Belgian stores plus shops in five other countries, spoiling stock. Many units were older models that no longer get updates.
items.action: List building controllers you own (HVAC, fridges, alarms, cameras), take any reachable from the internet offline or behind a VPN, and replace unsupported units.

items.title: Password manager mSecure tells all users to change their stored passwords
items.why: Maker mSeven Software emailed customers on November 3 about suspicious activity tied to the app and urged them to protect everything stored in it. It has not said what was accessed or whether vaults were exposed.
items.action: If anyone on your team uses mSecure, change the passwords it holds starting with banking and email, reset two-factor and passkeys, and consider moving to another manager.

items.title: CISA confirms attacks on the WordPress core update flaw fixed in 7.1.4
items.why: CISA added the WordPress core flaw that lets attackers run code during the brief window a site is updating to its exploited list on November 3. Versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 are affected; fixes cover every supported branch.
items.action: Check each WordPress site's version on the Updates screen, update to 7.1.4 or your branch's fixed release, and confirm agency- or host-managed sites were updated too.

items.title: Brazil's largest crypto exchange halts withdrawals after about $46 million drained
items.why: Mercado Bitcoin, with about 4.5 million customers, froze deposits and withdrawals after a cyberattack on November 2, days after the Binance theft. It says customers were not harmed; outside analysts say some customer wallets were emptied.
items.action: Keep business crypto in wallets you control or spread it across providers, require hardware-key sign-in on exchange accounts, and set withdrawal address allowlists.

items.title: Google takes down a 1.3 million-device botnet built into cheap Android TV boxes
items.why: Google says maker Videostrong deliberately shipped the x.cpe backdoor on set-top boxes, signage players and similar devices, including MECOOL-branded ones, and sold access for ad fraud and proxies. The backdoor survives restarts.
items.action: Find off-brand Android TV boxes and signage players on your network, check them against Synthient's model list, replace matches, and keep smart devices on a guest network.

items.title: Attackers drain hot wallets on older BTCPay Server installs
items.why: BTCPay Server says thieves are emptying Bitcoin and Litecoin hot wallets on merchant servers, with reports since November 1. Version 2.4.1 and earlier are at risk; the latest release, 2.4.7, has no credible drain reports.
items.action: If you take crypto through BTCPay, update to 2.4.7; on 2.4.1 or older, move to a fresh server and new wallet, and keep only operating funds in the hot wallet.

items.title: C3RB3R ransomware is encrypting Synology NAS boxes running old DSM versions
items.why: Synology warns attackers are exploiting a flaw it patched in December 2024 to encrypt files on outdated NAS devices and demand payment. Victims report paying thousands of dollars; over 380,000 Synology devices face the internet.
items.action: Update DSM to the latest build (7.2.2-72806-1 or later on 7.2.2), turn on automatic updates, and block the NAS admin page from the internet.

items.title: Public exploit released for already-exploited BeyondTrust Remote Support flaw
items.why: Rapid7 published a working attack module for the BeyondTrust Remote Support bug CISA flagged as exploited in October, and new probes have been seen against exposed appliances. Hosted customers were patched; self-hosted ones must act.
items.action: Apply BeyondTrust patch BT26-05-RS to self-hosted Remote Support now, limit who can reach the appliance, and check it for unknown PHP files or sessions.

items.title: Fake Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace planted SSH backdoors
items.why: Two tampered versions of the Claude Code extension were live on Cursor's marketplace for about 11 hours on October 29 and tried to add an attacker's SSH key and a hidden tunnel on Windows and Mac machines. Cursor says uninstalling alone is not enough.
items.action: Ask developers who use Cursor whether they installed Claude Code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313; if so, run Cursor's cleanup script, remove unknown SSH keys and rotate their credentials.

items.title: Northflank tells customers to rotate all secrets after AI API keys were abused
items.why: The cloud hosting platform says attackers may have read environment variables across workloads, secret groups and settings, and some customers' AI API keys were then used without permission. It ties the activity to a wider wave of AI credential theft.
items.action: If you deploy on Northflank, revoke and reissue every key, password and token stored there, then check your AI provider bills and usage logs for charges you don't recognize.

items.title: Chainalysis confirms hackers got into its internal tools
items.why: The blockchain analysis firm says an intruder using AI-driven tooling reached internal systems and saw customer users' names, emails and role labels. It says investigation data, passwords and session tokens were not accessed.
items.action: If you use Chainalysis, warn the named users to expect targeted phishing that uses their name and role, and confirm any unusual request by phone.

items.title: Polymarket theft traced to a hijacked page-speed script; refunds reach $2.7 million
items.why: New details: attackers took over the domain records of DebugBear, a monitoring vendor, and swapped its script on Polymarket's site to drain signed-in traders. Polymarket is refunding about $2.7 million to 726 wallets.
items.action: List the outside scripts on your login and checkout pages, remove ones you don't need, and pin the rest with Subresource Integrity so changed files are refused.

items.title: FBI confirms North Korea's TraderTraitor behind the $6.4 billion Binance hack
items.why: New tonight: the FBI formally blamed North Korea's TraderTraitor group, put the theft at $6.43 billion and published the thieves' wallets. About $2.85 billion is frozen; Binance began reopening withdrawals today.
items.action: If your business takes crypto payments, check incoming wallets against the FBI's published list, and keep exchange balances to what you need day to day.

items.title: Drupal Commerce flaw is being exploited against online stores
items.why: Drupal says attackers are abusing a missing-permission bug in Commerce Core, the module behind carts and checkout, and warns it can cost store owners money. Fixed releases are out.
items.action: Update Drupal Commerce Core to 3.3.13 (or 8.x-2.41 on older sites) today, then review recent orders and refunds for anything odd.

items.title: Fake IT help desk on Microsoft Teams led to full domain takeover
items.why: Microsoft says attackers posing as IT support on Teams talked staff into opening Quick Assist, then abused weak certificate settings to take over admin accounts and copy files out.
items.action: Block or limit Teams chats from outside companies, and tell staff IT will never ask them to start Quick Assist on an unexpected call.

items.title: CISA adds two more Ivanti VPN flaws to its exploited list
items.why: Update: CISA now lists two more Ivanti Connect Secure bugs used in the same attack chain as known exploited, with a federal fix deadline of November 2.
items.action: Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to 25.1.1.3 or 22.8R2.6 now and check the appliance for signs of earlier compromise.

items.title: MDaemon mail servers hacked through a booby-trapped attachment
items.why: ESET found attackers emailing a malicious RAR file to MDaemon servers; the built-in virus scanner opened it and planted malware with no one clicking anything. MDaemon 26.0.4 fixes it.
items.action: Update MDaemon to 26.0.4 or later, and confirm its bundled antivirus engine is current.

items.title: Hidden text message can crash Android phones and block calls
items.why: A researcher showed a single invisible SMS can crash the phone app on Pixel and Samsung devices running Android 12 to 17, cutting off calls including 911. No attacks seen yet; Google has a fix.
items.action: Check company Android phones for the October 2026 security patch or later, and plan to replace phones stuck on Android 12 or 13 that no longer get updates.

items.title: Binance plans staged withdrawal restart on Sunday as FBI investigates
items.why: Update: Binance says it has set aside $6.34 billion to cover the $6.3 billion theft and plans to restart withdrawals in stages on November 1 after security checks. The FBI and Secret Service are investigating; about $3 billion is frozen.
items.action: Assume one compromised device is rarely the whole story: after any incident, check every account and system that device could reach before declaring it contained.

items.title: Attackers are probing a new WordPress core flaw fixed in 7.1.4
items.why: A bug in the WordPress updater can let an outside attacker run code during a core upgrade. Wordfence logged tens of thousands of attempts within a day of the October 28 fix. It affects versions 4.7 through 7.1.3.
items.action: Update WordPress to 7.1.4 (or your branch's patched release) and confirm in the dashboard that the update installed rather than assuming auto-update ran.

items.title: Maximum-severity GitLab flaw is now exploited, CISA warns
items.why: CISA added a GitLab CI/CD flaw patched earlier this month to its exploited list on October 29. It can let an attacker run code on self-managed GitLab servers. Nearly 2,800 instances are exposed online.
items.action: Upgrade self-managed GitLab to 19.4.2, 19.3.5 or 19.2.8 or later, and run GitLab's new threat detections to check for signs of compromise.

items.title: TeamViewer fixes a flaw that lets a hostile host attack the person connecting
items.why: A bug in TeamViewer before 15.83 lets a malicious or compromised computer crash, and on Windows possibly take over, the viewer that connects to it for remote support. No attacks are known yet.
items.action: Update TeamViewer on every support and admin machine, including Portable and Android, to 15.83 or later, and update Host installs too since the same release fixes them.

items.title: Retailer Revolve says hackers took saved customer card numbers
items.why: In an SEC filing, Revolve said attackers used automated means to obtain names, contact details, card numbers and expiry dates saved in customer accounts. Texas filings list about 127,000 affected residents.
items.action: If you store customer cards, move to your payment processor's tokenized storage, and add login protections such as MFA and rate limiting to customer accounts.

items.title: Florida financial aid site breach exposes 4.9 million Social Security numbers
items.why: Florida's Department of Education says names, addresses, birth dates and Social Security numbers of nearly 5 million aid applicants were exposed. The site is offline and the state has not said how attackers got in.
items.action: Warn staff and families who applied for Florida aid to freeze their credit and watch for scam calls or emails that quote their personal details.

items.title: Binance freezes about $3 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen in its hack
items.why: Update: Binance says it has frozen just under half of the funds taken after a DevOps engineer's laptop was compromised. It will cover customer losses; Chainalysis and TRM Labs link the theft to North Korea.
items.action: Give admin and engineering laptops your strongest protection: phishing-resistant MFA, endpoint protection, and no standing access to production or money-moving systems.

items.title: PHP2Shell flaws now confirmed exploited, including on firewalls
items.why: Researchers report successful attacks on the two PHP runtime flaws patched October 21, including 24 compromised firewalls, and CISA has added them to its exploited list. Any server running PHP, including WordPress hosts, is in scope.
items.action: Update PHP to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or later (or ask your host to), restart the web server, and check internet-facing devices for web shells.

items.title: Cisco firewall VPN flaw is being used to knock devices offline
items.why: Cisco patched an actively exploited bug in ASA and FTD firewalls that lets an outside attacker crash the device when the SSL VPN uses secondary authentication.
items.action: Update Cisco ASA or FTD firewalls to Cisco's fixed release for your version, and check every VPN tunnel group, including the default one, for secondary authentication.

items.title: Ivanti ships more fixes for exploited Connect Secure VPN flaws
items.why: On October 29 Ivanti released patches for the remaining flaws in a chain attackers used to get root on its VPN and steal Active Directory credentials.
items.action: Upgrade Ivanti Connect Secure to 22.8R2.6 or 25.1.1.3, then reset the passwords of accounts the VPN uses to reach Active Directory.

items.title: Polymarket users lose about $2.1 million through a compromised website add-on
items.why: Polymarket says a third-party provider was breached; Hudson Rock found wallet-draining code in a DebugBear performance script embedded on the site. Polymarket removed the code and says affected traders will be repaid.
items.action: List every third-party script on your website and checkout pages, remove ones you no longer use, and restrict the rest with a Content Security Policy.

items.title: 319 Chrome extensions caught rerouting web searches
items.why: Researchers found extensions posing as PDF converters, safe-search and AI tools, with 13.4 million installs, sending searches through servers that could redirect users to phishing pages.
items.action: Review the Chrome extensions on work computers, remove PDF, search or security add-ons nobody needs, then run a full antivirus scan.

items.title: SafePay ransomware has hit 600+ organizations
items.why: A new FBI and CISA advisory says SafePay gets in through stolen or guessed passwords, VPN access and unpatched edge devices, then encrypts everything it can reach.
items.action: Turn on MFA for every account, starting with VPN and remote access, and keep an offline backup you have actually restored from.

items.title: Critical flaw in Veeam Backup & Replication 13
items.why: An unauthenticated attacker can bypass authorization checks in Veeam's backup server. Backups are the first thing ransomware crews go after.
items.action: Update to 13.1.2 or 13.0.3 now. Version 12 is not affected.

items.title: Microsoft ships emergency .NET security updates
items.why: Out-of-band fixes for .NET 8, 9 and 10 close a memory flaw and cover fixes the October patch release missed.
items.action: Update .NET on your servers, then rebuild any self-contained apps, since they carry their own copy.
